q: Conley's fundamental theorem of dynamical systems states that any flow on a compact space decomposes into:
opts: Chain-recurrent set (attractor-free dynamics) and gradient-like part flowing between chain-recurrent pieces
exp: Conley decomposition: X = CR(T) ∪ {points flowing between chain-recurrent pieces}. There exists a Lyapunov function (Conley-Lyapunov function) that is constant on chain-recurrent pieces and strictly decreasing on connecting orbits. This is the 'fundamental theorem of dynamical systems'.
